findings.summary: The actively-used @anthropic-ai/sdk dependency is pinned with a caret on a 0.x version, which cannot adopt fixes published outside the 0.104.* patch line.
findings.evidence: dependencies: "@anthropic-ai/sdk": "^0.104.1". Under semver, a caret on a 0.x package resolves to >=0.104.1 <0.105.0, so any security or correctness fix shipped in 0.105.0+ is unreachable without a manual manifest edit. The package is genuinely in use: files/src/main/claudeAssistant.ts:4 has `import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';`.
findings.recommendation: Widen the range to `~0.104` only as a stopgap and add @anthropic-ai/sdk to a Renovate/Dependabot config so 0.x minor bumps are raised as PRs automatically; re-pin deliberately at each minor rather than relying on caret resolution.

findings.summary: index.html loads @tabler/icons-webfont from a third-party CDN at the floating `@latest` tag with no subresource integrity, duplicating a dependency that is already declared and bundled.
findings.evidence: files/index.html:8: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tabler/icons-webfont@latest/tabler-icons.min.css" />`. The same package is declared in dependencies as "@tabler/icons-webfont": "^3.44.0" and imported through the bundler at files/src/renderer/index.tsx:3. The CDN copy is outside the lockfile entirely: `@latest` resolves to whatever jsdelivr serves at load time, and there is no `integrity` attribute to detect substitution.
findings.recommendation: Delete the CDN <link> from files/index.html and rely on the bundled `import '@tabler/icons-webfont/dist/tabler-icons.min.css'` that already exists, so the stylesheet is covered by package-lock.json.

findings.summary: The repository has no CI pipeline, no vulnerability-scan step, and no Renovate or Dependabot configuration, so no dependency update or advisory is surfaced automatically.
findings.evidence: None of .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, .circleci/config.yml, renovate.json, .dependabot/config.yml, or .github/dependabot.yml exist in the repository. package.json scripts contains only dev/watch:main/watch:renderer/build/dist/typecheck/gen:dtcs — there is no `audit` or test entry. This is the root cause behind several stale majors that would otherwise be reported separately: "react": "^18.0.0" and "react-dom": "^18.0.0" (React 19 is the current line), "zustand": "^4.0.0" (v5 is current), and "electron-store": "^8.0.0" (several majors behind). Each is one boundary or more behind and none can advance on its own, because a caret range never crosses a major.
findings.recommendation: Add a .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs `npm ci` followed by `npm audit --audit-level=high` and `npm run typecheck`, and commit a renovate.json (or .github/dependabot.yml) so major-version bumps such as react 18→19 and zustand 4→5 arrive as reviewable PRs.

findings.summary: electron-store is declared as a runtime dependency but is never imported anywhere in the source tree.
findings.evidence: dependencies: "electron-store": "^8.0.0". A recursive search across every .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.html/.css file under files/ (excluding node_modules and package-lock.json) returns zero occurrences of the string `electron-store` — no `import`, no `require`, not even a comment. Persistence is instead handled by better-sqlite3 in files/src/main/storageService.ts:45. The declared ^8.0.0 is also several majors behind current, which is moot if the package is removed.
findings.recommendation: Remove "electron-store" from dependencies in files/package.json and regenerate package-lock.json.

findings.summary: package.json declares no `engines` field, leaving the Node and npm versions used to build the app unconstrained.
findings.evidence: There is no `engines` key anywhere in files/package.json. This matters more than usual here because the project depends on better-sqlite3 (^12.11.1), a native module whose prebuilt binaries are tied to a specific Node/Electron ABI, and it is packaged with electron-builder (^26.15.3). A contributor on a mismatched Node major can produce a silently broken native build.
findings.recommendation: Add an `engines` block to files/package.json pinning the supported runtime, e.g. `"engines": {"node": ">=22 <23", "npm": ">=10"}`, matching the @types/node ^22.0.0 already declared.

findings.summary: package.json has no `overrides` block, so a vulnerable transitive dependency cannot be pinned without waiting for every direct parent to publish a fix.
findings.evidence: No `overrides` (npm) or `resolutions` (yarn) key is present in files/package.json. The dependency surface that sits below the direct deps is large — package-lock.json is 357790 bytes — and deep toolchain trees such as webpack ^5, electron-builder ^26 and ts-node ^10 are exactly where transitive advisories land.
findings.recommendation: Add an empty `"overrides": {}` block to files/package.json as a documented emergency lever, so a transitive pin is a one-line edit during an incident rather than a structural change.

findings.summary: recharts is declared as a runtime dependency but is never imported anywhere in the source tree.
findings.evidence: dependencies: "recharts": "^2.0.0". A recursive search across every .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.html/.css file under files/ (excluding node_modules and package-lock.json) returns zero occurrences of the string `recharts`, including in the charting-heavy screens under files/src/renderer/screens/ such as LiveScreen.tsx and HealthScreen.tsx.
findings.recommendation: Remove "recharts" from dependencies in files/package.json and regenerate package-lock.json; re-add it deliberately if charting is reintroduced.
